Recently, simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) and renewable energy cooperation are potential to achieve lasting and green information transmitting and processing by making full use of the energy from radio frequency (RF) signal and renewable energy. In this paper, a joint renewable energy cooperation, transmission power allocation and power splitting scheme is studied under a hybrid power supplied SWIPT system. Considering WAPs’ battery capacity and LPIDs’ heterogeneous service requirement, a service-driven grid power expenditure minimization problem is formulated. To solve this non-smooth and non-convex problem, an adaptive power scheduling and splitting algorithm (APSSA) with low computational complexity is proposed by analyzing the explicit relationship between power splitting and transmission power and the demand features of renewable energy cooperation. Extensive simulation results show that our APSSA 1) extends all LPIDs’ battery life by achieving an effective trade-off between information decoding and energy harvesting; 2) reduces the grid power expenditure by adopting renewable energy cooperation.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Covert Communication in Underlay Cognitive Radio Networks with Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: This paper examines covert communication in underlay cognitive radio networks (CRNs) with energy harvesting (EH), in which considers two scenarios: 1) with perfect channel state information (CSI) of the link from the secondary source (SS) to the primary receiver (PR) at Willie, 2) with statistical CSI of the SS-PR link at Willie. The closed-form expressions for Willie’s detection error probability, the average minimum detection error probability, the transmission outage probability, and the maximum effective covert rate under both cases are derived and analyzed. The maximum effective covert rate is obtained by optimizing the maximum jamming power of the primary transmitter (PT). The numerical results demonstrate that the combined effect of energy conversion efficiency and time allocation ratio of EH, in conjunction with the maximum jamming power of PT, provides a positive effective covert rate in the secondary network. Furthermore, it is evident that the maximum effective covert rate in the secondary network is greater when Willie has access to the perfect CSI of the SS-PR link than that when Willie only has access to the statistical CSI of the SS-PR link.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Iterative and Deep Fusion Frameworks for Enhanced Passive DOA Sensing via a Green Massive H2AD MIMO Receiver
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Most existing DOA estimation methods assume ideal source incident angles with minimal noise. Moreover, directly using pre-estimated angles to calculate weighted coefficients can lead to performance loss. Thus, a green multi-modal (MM) fusion DOA framework is proposed to realize a more practical, low-cost and high time-efficiency DOA estimation for a HAD array. Firstly, two more efficient clustering methods, global maximum cos_similarity clustering (GMaxCS) and global minimum distance clustering (GMinD), are presented to infer more precise true solutions from the candidate solution sets. Based on this, an iteration weighted fusion (IWF)-based method is introduced to iteratively update weighted fusion coefficients and the clustering center of the true solution classes by using the estimated values. Particularly, the coarse DOA calculated by fully digital (FD) subarray, serves as the initial cluster center. The above process yields two methods called MM-IWF-GMaxCS and MM-IWF-GMinD. To further provide a higher-accuracy DOA estimation, a fusion network (fusionNet) is proposed to aggregate the inferred two-part true angles and thus generates two effective approaches called MM-fusionNet-GMaxCS and MM-fusionNet-GMinD. The simulation outcomes show the proposed four approaches can achieve the ideal DOA performance and the CRLB. Meanwhile, proposed MM-fusionNet-GMaxCS and MM-fusionNet-GMinD exhibit superior DOA performance compared to MM-IWF-GMaxCS and MM-IWF-GMinD, especially in extremely-low SNR range.

articleTitle: Cooperative Reinforcement Learning for Energy Management in Multi-Hop Networks With Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: This paper proposes a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for joint transmit-sleep scheduling for multi-hops wireless sensor and IoT networks with energy harvesting. The goal of the framework is to learn situation-specific scheduling policies for reducing energy expenditure, while maintaining network performance in terms of packet delivery ratio and end-to-end delay. The proposed system uses a cooperative RL approach where two learning agents, deployed per node, jointly learn transmit and sleep scheduling strategies to manage network energy budgets. The RL framework also uses a localized learning confidence parameter sharing strategy that allows the nodes to ignore unreliable RL observations. This makes the system scalable for network topologies where the source and destination nodes are separated by many numbers of hops. The learning module is decentralized in that learning is independently carried out at the sensor/IoT nodes without relying on a central learning coordinator. Decentralized learning makes the system computationally efficient, and also avoids energy and communication bandwidth overhead usually imposed by a central coordinator. With simulation studies, the proposed learning-driven protocol is tested and compared against existing known MAC sleep schedulers. The proposed mechanism is validated for different scenarios with heterogeneous topologies, traffic, and energy harvesting conditions.

articleTitle: Performance of Partitioning Enabled IRS-Assisted NOMA Network with Opportunistic User Relaying
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: This paper investigates a partition-based intelligent reflective surface (IRS) aided cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access (C-NOMA) framework where the source communicates with a near user (NU) and a far user (FU). Based on one-bit feedback from the users, opportunistic mode switching among non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), orthogonal multiple access (OMA), and C-NOMA modes is performed to ensure that the NU does not compromise on its performance for cooperating with FU. To minimize energy expenditure at the NU, the IRS is also utilized in the second phase with C-NOMA in this novel signalling scheme. Both co-phasing (COP) that requires channel feedback, and random phase shifting (RPS) without channel feedback are considered. Closed-form expressions are derived for NU and FU throughput. We demonstrate that the choice of power allocation coefficient and partitioning is crucial, but the difficult two-dimensional search is reduced to a simple one-dimensional one over integer parameter, greatly reducing the search complexity. The suggested scheme ensures higher throughput, user fairness, and energy efficiency in comparison to the frameworks with fixed transmission modes, and those that do not use the IRS in the second phase of signalling. The derived analytical expressions are validated by Monte Carlo simulations.=-1

articleTitle: A Hybrid Noise Approach to Modelling of Free-Space Satellite Quantum Communication Channel for Continuous-Variable QKD
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: This research advances the application of QKD in FSO satellite-based quantum communication. It proposes an innovative satellite quantum channel model and derives the secret quantum key distribution rate achievable through this channel. Unlike existing models that approximate the noise in quantum channels as merely Gaussian distributed, this model incorporates a hybrid quantum noise analysis, accounting for both quantum Poissonian noise and classical AWGN. This hybrid approach acknowledges the dual vulnerability of CV Gaussian quantum channels to both quantum and classical noise under collective attack with RR setting, thereby offering a more realistic assessment of the quantum SKR. This work delves into the variation of asymptotic SKR with the SNR and satellite altitudes under various influencing parameters. We identify and analyze critical factors such as reconciliation efficiency, electrical noise, transmission coefficient, detection efficiency, transmission efficiency, excess noise, and the quantum Poissonian noise parameter impacting the SKR. These parameters are pivotal in determining the asymptotic SKR in FSO satellite quantum channels, highlighting the challenges of satellite-based quantum communication. A comparative study has been provided based on the finite-size and asymptotic SKR. It provides a comprehensive framework for understanding and optimizing asymptotic SKR in satellite-based QKD systems, paving the way for more efficient and secure quantum communication networks.

articleTitle: Learning Automata Based Routing and Data Dissemination for Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) have enormous potential for exploring oceans that cover more than 70% of the earth. In UWSN, sensor nodes are deployed in a three-dimensional water region which is characterized by water depth, and continuously disseminate real-time underwater data to sink nodes through multi-hop communication. Due to mobility and limited energy of sink/sensor nodes, multi-hop marine data routing and dissemination suffer from long data transmission latency and low delivery ratios. In this paper, we propose a learning automata based routing and data dissemination framework for UWSN, and aim to reduce real-time underwater data access delays and improve data delivery ratios. The framework leverages learning automata to construct routing paths so that underwater data can be continuously delivered to sink nodes by reusing routing paths and supporting sink/sensor node mobility. The simulation results demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Quantum Error Correction in Green Communications: Towards Sustainable Quantum Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: This work explores the integration of Quantum Error Correction (QEC) techniques within energy-efficient green communication networks, emphasizing their pivotal role in achieving sustainability in next-generation Information and Communication Technology (ICT) systems. Quantum technologies, particularly error correction protocols like surface codes are indispensable for reliable quantum information processing. However, their implementation often incurs substantial energy overhead due to the extensive physical qubit resources required. This research proposes a framework for adapting scalable QEC algorithms, leveraging innovations such as reconfigurable atom arrays, to optimize energy consumption while preserving high fidelity in quantum operations. Surface codes, a cornerstone of QEC, encode logical qubits in two-dimensional lattices of physical qubits, utilizing stabilizer measurements to detect and correct bit-flip and phase-flip errors. The performance of surface codes is influenced by critical parameters such as code distance, which determines fault tolerance, and gate fidelity, which impacts logical error rates. Through a comprehensive analysis of these parameters, this work evaluates the interplay between code distance, qubit array size, and gate fidelity to highlight their collective impact on fault tolerance and computational accuracy. These insights align with global efforts to reduce the environmental footprint of emerging quantum technologies, advancing the principles of green ICT and environmentally conscious innovation.

articleTitle: AWB-FCNN Algorithm for Mainlobe Interference Suppression
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: As one of the promising technologies of wideband beamforming, the anti-mainlobe interference wideband beamforming (AWB) algorithm can effectively suppress mainlobe distortion and sidelobe level rise, thereby improving the output signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR) performance. Therefore, an AWB algorithm is proposed via a feature fusion convolutional neural network (FCNN) in this paper, named as AWB-FCNN algorithm. It can improve the beamforming performance and ensure the computational efficiency. For this algorithm, an AWB algorithm firstly is used to generate the network training label. Then, an FCNN model is constructed to predict beamforming weight vectors, which consists of a feature extraction module, a feature fusion module, and a weight vector prediction module. Specially, an atrous convolution layer is introduced into the feature extraction module to extract dense features, which be achieved by enlarging the receptive field without increasing the parameters of the network. Besides, the feature fusion module is used to reduce the irrelevant features such as mainlobe interference by fusing features at different scales. Finally, the well-trained FCNN model can rapidly and precisely output beamforming weight vectors. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has excellent interference suppression ability and high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Resource Allocation for Intelligent Solar Aware Cellular Base Stations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: In response to the global climate crisis, solar-powered cellular base stations (BSs) are increasingly attractive to mobile network operators as a green solution to reduce the carbon footprint of networks. However, solar power presents challenges due to its diurnal nature and significant variations in harvestable power due to weather changes. To address these challenges, solar deployments rely on batteries to provide power during the night and periods of low sunlight. Batteries are expensive and have complex environmental considerations, making it desirable to minimize their use at each BS and avoid over-provisioning. Accurate prediction of energy income is essential to minimize the number of Photovoltaic (PV) panels and batteries required while maintaining the quality of service (QoS), achieve a desired energy outage probability, for users. This paper introduces an innovative approach to predict energy harvesting by utilizing a novel conditional Long Short-Term Memory (Cond-LSTM) neural network architecture. Compared with standard LSTM and Transformer models, the Cond-LSTM model reduced the normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) by 69.6% and 42.7%, respectively. The proposed approach facilitates an accurate, cost-optimal PV-battery configuration that meets outage probability requirements and aids in site design for regions lacking historical solar energy data. Additionally, we propose a solar-aware cellular communication scheme and user power allocation to enhance QoS via signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) optimization and minimize the probability of energy outages in the cellular system. Simulation results show the efficiency of our proposed solar aware model in decreasing the overall outage probability of the system and increasing the data throughput of the cellular system. For the same battery configuration, our algorithm achieves 60 percent smaller outage probability and 8 billion bps greater data throughput than a non solar aware approach.

articleTitle: Trade-Off Between Renewable Energy Utilizing and Communication Quality for Base Stations: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Safe RL Method
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: The ultra-dense deployment of base stations (BSs) results in significant energy costs, while the increasing use of fluctuating renewable energy sources (RESs) threatens the safe operation of electric network (EN). These issues can be addressed by coordinating BSs’ active/sleep states with RES generation. However, the coordinated decision-making is challenging due to the conflicting goals of maximizing RES utilization, guaranteeing communication quality of service (QoS). In this paper, we design an electric-cellular collaborative network (ECCN) and formulate a joint optimization problem to minimize electric supply and QoS degradation costs, subjecting to EN’s safety constraints. Considering the uncertainty of RES generation and BS traffic, we propose a heterogeneous multi-agent safe reinforcement learning (HMAS-RL) algorithm to solve the problem. HMAS-RL inherits from the centralized critic and decentralized actor framework, where two heterogeneous agents learn a cooperative policy for joint decision-making through two actor networks design that share observations and a team reward. A cost critic network is designed to handle safety constraints, eliminating the need for manual penalty term design and tuning. We validate the proposed method using an IEEE 33-bus electric distribution test feeder. Results demonstrate HMAS-RL achieves superior performance in RES utilization, communication QoS, and EN safety constraints maintenance.

articleTitle: Energy- and Latency-Efficient Resource Allocation for RIS-Assisted UAV-USV Cooperative MEC Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: The potential of cooperative unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-unmanned surface vehicle (USV) multi-access edge computing (MEC) platform cannot be fully revealed without thoroughly investigating USVs bidirectional data computation. In this paper, a novel reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted UAV-USV cooperative MEC network architecture is proposed considering USVs bidirectional tasks with hard time window. The weighted sum minimization of UAVs energy consumption and task execution latency is formulated by jointly considering USVs task execution mode selection indicators, UAVs flight route indicators, UAVs arrival time, UAVs hovering coordinates and RIS phase shift vector. A heuristic solution is proposed to solve the formulated challenging problem, where we divide the original problem into three subproblems, i.e., UAVs flight route indicators subproblem, the joint task execution mode selection indicators and UAVs arrival time subproblem and the joint UAVs hovering coordinates and RIS phase shift vector design subproblem; each of which is solved by the proposed enhanced grey wolf optimizer (EGWO) algorithm, the integer constrained-removed augmented Lagrangian (ICRAL) algorithm and the proposed multi-objective differential evolution (MODE) algorithm, respectively. The results verify that the proposed solution can significantly decrease the weighted sum of UAVs energy consumption and task execution latency in comparison with numerous selected advanced algorithms.

articleTitle: Multi-Round Stackelberg Game-Based Pricing and Offloading in Containerized MEC Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) tackles the challenges associated with the rapid proliferation of User Equipment (UE) and limited computing resources. Containerization, essential for MEC deployments, encapsulates applications and dependencies, optimizing resource utilization. In containerized MEC networks, UEs offload computational tasks to edge server containers, enabling service providers to profit from offering scalable and portable services, thereby establishing a symbiotic economic ecosystem. However, traditional models, which often separate cost and delay assessments, fail to consider these factors holistically. Furthermore, they underutilize the potential of container images’ hierarchical structure, which could optimize storage and reduce costs. Our research introduces a novel multi-round Stackelberg game framework that incorporates the hierarchical structure of container images to enhance resource management in MEC networks. Additionally, we integrate discount rates to model long-term economic interactions accurately, and develop two innovative algorithms: the Distributed Ant Colony Pricing (DACP) and the Multi-Round Simulated Annealing Pricing (MRSAP). These algorithms account for both immediate and long-term impacts, redefining user utility and significantly improving system efficiency. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of our algorithms in optimizing resource allocation and enhancing efficiency in dynamic MEC scenarios.

articleTitle: Power Allocation & CAR Optimization in Multiuser Dual-hop RF/FSO DF Relaying Systems with Channel Estimation Error
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: In this work we study the up-link transmission performance of multi-user dual-hop radio frequency (RF)/ free space optical (FSO) relaying system considering imperfect channel state information (CSI) at RF link and FSO link. It involves users transmitting signals to the relay via RF links affected by Rayleigh fading, followed by relay forwarding the decoded signal to the destination through an FSO link encountering turbulence characterized by the Fisher Snedecor (F) distribution. To ensure fairness, a cumulative distribution function based scheduling (CDFS) scheme is employed for user selection. Analytical expression for outage probability (OP) is derived, considering independent and non-identically distributed (i.n.i.d) co-channel interference (CCI). Asymptotic expression is also formulated for high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to gain insights. Additionally, optimal power allocation coefficient and optimum channel access ratio (CAR) values are obtained to enhance system performance. We have considered three scenarios: Imperfect RF link only, Imperfect FSO link only and imperfect RF & FSO link. Results indicate that outage performance achieved with imperfect RF & FSO link and imperfect FSO link only, is similar which indicates that the imperfect FSO link severely affects the performance. Further, our findings reveal that under imperfect RF link only, power allocation can substantially improve system outage over a broad range of interference power and data rates. CDFS-based scheduling with power allocation demonstrates significant performance improvement in comparison to greedy scheduling scheme. Monte-Carlo simulation are conducted to verify the accuracy of our analytical findings.

articleTitle: Supporting Massive IoT Connectivity With Sectorized Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: We explore the feasibility of supporting a huge number, K, of concurrent Internet of Things (IoT) connections, using a sectorized Massive MIMO base station (BS) equipped with M service antennas where K is much larger than M. Due to the limited length of the coherence interval, only τp resources are available for uplink reference signals (RSs) that provide τp orthogonal RSs. When K is much larger than τp, the orthogonal uplink RSs must be reused or random non-orthogonal RSs can be utilized to accommodate the large number IoT connections. In this severe RS contamination scenario, we consider sectorization to enhance network performance. If we divide a circular cell into S sectors and using M/Sdirectional antennas per sector, the effective array gain reduces to M/S. However, this loss is more than compensated by the reduction of RS congestion, leading to a substantial increase in spectral efficiency (SE) as S increases. Given the large number of IoT devices, we increase the number of sectors to uncover some useful characteristics of the sectorization to support massive IoT connections with Massive MIMO. We derive a theoretical approximation of SE and propose a simple and effective scheme that determine the number of sectors for given performance requirements. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve around 48% of SE improvement compared to the conventional scheme.

articleTitle: Stackelberg Game for Cognitive Ambient Backscatter Network with Perfect and Imperfect Spectrum Sensing
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: The combination of cognitive radio and ambient backscatter communication can effectively improve spectrum utilization and reduce power consumption. However, when multiple backscatter devices coexist in this network, the competition among secondary backscatter users (SBUs) and conflict of interest in licensed bands due to spectrum sharing are issues that cannot be ignored. In this paper, we study the Stackelberg game to achieve a win-win transmission between primary users (PUs) and SBUs in the sensing-based cognitive ambient backscatter network. The sensing-based dual bandwidth pricing mechanisms under perfect spectrum sensing and imperfect spectrum sensing are proposed, respectively. For the perfect spectrum sensing scenario, resource allocation optimization algorithms based on the Stackelberg game are formulated to maximize the bandwidth revenue of primary users and the throughput utility function of SBUs. For the imperfect spectrum sensing scenario, hybrid transmission modes and the interference to legacy links based on different detection results are considered. Furthermore, the non-convex optimization problem based on the Stackelberg game is solved in closed-form expressions by corresponding theoretical derivation. Simulation results show that the proposed pricing mechanisms can effectively improve the revenue of primary users and the throughput performance of SBUs.

articleTitle: Mobility Management in Low-Altitude Cell-Free Radio Access Network
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Cell-free networks offer promising solutions for achieving low-altitude coverage through the large-scale deployment of access points (APs). However, the high mobility of unmanned aerial vehicle users (UAV-UEs) and the non-scalability of cell-free networks pose challenges for mobility management. In this paper, we focus on full-spectrum cell-free radio access networks (CF-RAN) with scalability. Through a multi-objective optimization design for the handover process, we effectively address the mobility management challenges of high-speed UAV-UEs in a low-altitude CF-RAN. First, we propose a hybrid user-and-network-centric (HUNC) initial access algorithm for UEs. Based on direction prediction, this algorithm facilitates the initial association between UEs and edge distributed units (EDUs), as well as between UEs and APs in a full-spectrum CF-RAN architecture. Next, we innovatively formulate a multi-objective optimization problem to balance the uplink achievable rate and the handover frequency in the AP handover phase. Then, we employ an enhanced non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) developed within a fuzzy decision framework (FDV) to achieve dynamic optimal AP handovers. Finally, Simulation results show that our proposed scheme effectively balances communication performance and handover overhead, achieving comparable performance to the user-centric (UC) handover approach while reducing handover frequency, making it well-suited for multi-UAV low-altitude scenarios.

articleTitle: Channel Characteristics-Based Domain Adaptation for Multiuser MISO Beamforming With Transformer and Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Deep learning-based beamforming solutions face the issue of channel mismatch when the communication environment changes. Although existing adaptive solutions, such as meta-learning, can solve the channel mismatch, they still have some disadvantages. First, they rely on labelled data in the fine-tuning stage. Second, the characteristics of channel state information (CSI) has not been fully explored and transferred, which are important for improving adaptation performance. Third, these works are based on traditional artificial neural networks (ANNs) and have high energy cost. To address these challenges, the paper first proposes a novel domain adaptation framework based on channel correlation characteristics for sum rate maximization (SRM), named DA-SRM, which does not require labelled data during the transfer process. Then, two transformer units with different attention mechanism are applied to explore the long-range dependence characteristics of CSI. Finally, energy-efficient spiking neural networks (SNNs) versions are proposed to reduce the energy cost of traditional ANNs. Simulation results show that the proposed DA-SRM and transformer-based DA-SRM achieve better adaptation performance than existing beamforming adaptive solutions. In addition, compared to the ANNs-based solutions, the proposed SNNs versions reduce the energy cost by more than ten times.

articleTitle: Iterative PAPR Reduction Scheme with Optimized Phase Pre-Distortion Sequence for OTFS Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: To achieve the expected peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction of orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) signals and thus improve the energy efficiency of the power amplifier in practical systems, we propose an iterative PAPR reduction scheme with phase pre-distortion sequences for the embedded-pilot OTFS system. In the proposed scheme, each large peak in the time domain is searched and its corresponding symbols in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain (i.e., a vector in the Doppler domain) are multiplied with the phase pre-distortion sequence and the pre-distortion sequence is optimized to minimize the introduced linear distortions (only phase distortions without amplitude distortions) with the expected PAPR constraint. The optimized phase pre-distortion sequence is determined by exhaustive search or pre-trained Random Forest from the available pre-distortion sequence set. If the pilot is distorted by the phase sequence, its position in the DD domain is used to transmit the information about its phase distortion and can be detected by the variance of the amplitude in all available embedded-pilot regions at the receiver. Simulation results demonstrate that the gain of PAPR reduction in our scheme is about 3.6dB over the conventional OTFS signals when complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) is 10-4 with negligible bit error rate (BER) degradation, which is much superior to the modified Iterative Clipping Filtering (m-ICF) scheme.

articleTitle: Graph Pointer Network Assisted Deep Reinforcement Learning for Virtualized Network Embedding
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Network Function Virtualization (NFV) improves the flexibility and scalability of network services and reduces operating costs. As the core of research on network virtualization, Virtual Network Embedding (VNE) aims to effectively deploy service requests on physical network components and allocate underlying physical resources. However, network services can be complex and diverse, which makes it difficult for existing embedding methods to effectively utilize the graph structure of services, tackle the complexity of dynamic networks, and provide effective embedding solutions. To this end, we propose GPRL, an online VNE method based on graph pointer network and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). By combining the graph neural network and pointer network, we design a novel graph pointer network as the DRL agent. It employs the graph attention network to encode graph feature data and decodes to output the embedding policy via the pointer network architecture. Furthermore, the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm is used to effectively train the designed agent. The effectiveness and superiority of GPRL are verified by simulation experiments, and GPRL is shown to perform better than existing embedding methods.

articleTitle: GAS: DVFS-Driven Energy Efficiency Approach for Latency-Guaranteed Edge Computing Microservices
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Edge computing-based microservices (ECM) are pivotal infrastructure components for latency-critical applications such as Virtual Reality/Augmented Reality (VR/AR) and the Internet of Things (IoT). ECM involves strategically deploying microservices at the network’s edge to fulfill the low latency needs of modern applications. However, achieving efficient resource and energy consumption while meeting the latency requirement in the ECM environment remains challenging. Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS) is a common technique to address this issue. It adjusts the CPU frequency and voltage to balance energy cost and performance. However, selecting the optimal CPU frequency depends on the nature of the microservice workload (e.g., CPU-bound, memory-bound, or mixed). Moreover, various microservices with different latency requirement can be deployed on the same edge node. This makes the DVFS application extremely challenging, particularly for a chip-wide DVFS implementation for which CPU cores operate at the same frequency and voltage. To this end, we propose GAS, enerGy Aware microServices edge computing framework, which enables CPU frequency scaling to meet diverse microservice latency requirement with the minimum energy cost. Our evaluation indicates that our CPU scaling policy decreases energy consumption by 5% to 23% compared to Linux governors while maintaining latency requirement and significantly contributing to sustainable edge computing.

articleTitle: On the Optimal Trade-off of Delay and Energy Consumption in 3C-Enabled F-RAN
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: In order to improve the flexibility and resilience of network service provision under constrained resources, a joint scheduling of communication-computation-caching (3C) is investigated. Focusing on the application of adaptive bit-rate (ABR) content streaming, a 3C-enabled fog radio access network (F-RAN) is established in the first place. Within the proposed architecture of 3C-enabled F-RAN for ABR, the sequential arrivals and processing of users’ content requests are modeled as a multi-class processor queue. On this basis, the average delay and energy consumption in downloading a requested content are respectively analyzed and obtained in closed-form expressions. For optimizing these two performance metrics separately, alternating direction method of multipliers-based algorithms are proposed by efficiently utilizing the available 3C resources. Since these two metrics cannot be optimized simultaneously, in order to characterize the optimal performance trade-off between them, an evolutionary multitasking-based constrained multi-objective optimization-based algorithm is proposed to solve the Pareto frontier. The proposed algorithm is more robust to population size and converges faster as compared to the state-of-the-art methods. Simulation results demonstrate the obtained Pareto frontier between delay and energy consumption, illustrating an inherent performance trade-off between them. With a coordinated allocation of 3C, customized services can be provided while avoiding unnecessary waste of resources.

articleTitle: Online Power Scheduling for Energy Harvesting RTU in 5G-Enabled Cyber-Physical Power System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: The 5G network provides an appealing communication platform for the cyber-physical power system (CPPS) in support of wide access of terminals and tremendous sensing data transmission. In the meantime, the remote terminal unit (RTU) plays a salient role in sensing operation data and executing control commands in CPPS, which, however, usually suffers from energy scarcity. The 5G network provides an appealing communication platform for the cyber-physical power system (CPPS), enabling the transmission of tremendous sensing data from remote terminal units (RTUs). To address the issue of energy scarcity faced by RTUs, this paper presents an energy-harvesting RTU model for data sensing and transmission in 5G-enabled CPPS. A hybrid energy source scenario is investigated, where renewable energy is harvested from the surroundings while grid energy is used as supplementary. Then the RTU power scheduling issue is formulated to minimize the energy cost under the constraints of long-term queuing delay and average energy storage. Given the problem is NP-hard due to information uncertainty, Lyapunov optimization is adopted to transform it into a series of short-term power scheduling subproblems. Furthermore, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) based power scheduling algorithm (TD3-PER-OPSA) is developed to facilitate online power scheduling decisions. Extensive experimental evaluations using real-world solar power generation data demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves the optimal energy-communication tradeoff and outperforms benchmark methods in terms of training convergence, energy cost, and transmission performance.

articleTitle: Utility Driven Digital Twin Deployment for Energy-Efficient Industrial Edge Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Promoted by 6G technologies, the Digital Twin Edge Network (DITEN) has profoundly transformed the production and manufacturing mode. Through synchronization and interaction between industrial equipment and digital twin (DT), the DITEN has significantly improved the operational efficiency of complex industrial systems with enhanced timeliness and energy efficiency. However, as an important precondition, the rational DT deployment associating DT models with edge servers should be investigated in an optimal fashion. Failing to adequately address both immediate response and sustainable service, the existing approaches are difficult to effectively satisfy the stringent requirements of low-latency and energy-efficiency in industrial scenarios, and continuously improve the DITEN service performance. To address those critical challenges, with the distinct performance requirements of DT models and edge servers, both short-term and long-term utilities are respectively defined, and an optimization problem of utility-aware DT model deployment is formulated to jointly balance short-term and long-term utilities in the decision-making. With the proof that the investigation is a Markov Decision Process (MDP) problem, an Intrinsic-Curiosity-empowered Multi Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (IC-MAPPO) algorithm is designed to offer a promising solution. Simulation results show that the utility balance could be ensured by latency effectiveness, energy-efficiency, and balanced workload.

articleTitle: Opportunistic Routing in Drone-Augmented Mobile Social Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Mobile social network (MSN) technologies are producing viable solutions to many critical scenarios, including disaster recovery, mobile crowdsourcing, mobile file caching, mobile agent systems, and so on. MSN performance as well as practices can be further improved by drones, which are small battery-powered unmanned aerial vehicles. However, to the best of our knowledge, there is no routing protocol designed for drone-augmented MSNs. Therefore, in this paper, we first introduce a new routing paradigm, called drone-augmented opportunistic routing for landmark-based MSNs. By incorporating the random mobility of mobile nodes as well as the deterministic mobility of drones, the opportunistic path model is defined. The key idea of our path model is the reduction to anycast-like routing to multiple destinations with different deadlines, in which the high mobility of drones is exploited. Then, we propose the drone-augmented opportunistic routing (DAOR) protocol, which forwards messages along the path with the smallest weight based on the greedy strategy. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DAOR achieves its design goals.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation for IoT Communication in A Full-Duplex NOMA-SR System With α-Fairness Principle
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Addressing the challenges of spectrum scarcity, excessive energy consumption, and the need for extensive green coverage in the future Internet of Things (IoT), this paper integrates full-duplex (FD), symbiotic radio (SR), and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technologies. Considering non-linear energy harvesting (EH), channel estimation errors, and residual self-interference (RSI) in FD, we establish an FD-based NOMA-SR transmission model. To maximize the total throughput of backscatter devices (BDs) within the framework of the α-fairness utility function, we construct a non-convex optimization function subject to minimum throughput requirements of FD access points (FAPs), BDs’ harvested energy constraints, total transmission power constraints, and other practical limitations. To solve this problem, the original optimization function is first transformed into three sub-optimization problems. Subsequently, leveraging quadratic transformation and convex-concave programming, these non-convex sub-optimization problems are converted into solvable convex optimization problems. Finally, based on the principle of alternating iteration, a joint optimization of NOMA cluster time slot allocation, BDs’ reflection coefficients (RCs), and FAPs’ power allocation is developed. Numerical simulation results validate the convergence and effectiveness of the proposed resource allocation scheme. Moreover, compared to half-duplex (HD)-based NOMA-SR and FD-based time division multiple access (TDMA)-SR schemes, the proposed transmission scheme demonstrates superior throughput performance under different fairness level requirements.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Semi-Passive IRS Phase Shifts and NOMA Power Coefficients for Cooperative CRNs
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: We investigate the incorporation of an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) into cooperative spectrum-sharing cognitive radio networks (CRNs). The CRN consists of a primary user (PU) and multiple secondary users (SUs). There are two transmission phases. In the first phase, the primary transmitter is assisted by an IRS to serve the primary user (PU). This arrangement allows the primary network to allocate a part of its spectrum to the users within the secondary network. In the subsequent phase, the secondary transmitter (ST) employs a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) transmission technique to simultaneously serve the PU and secondary users (SUs). By utilizing a semi-passive IRS, both data transmission to the PU and channel estimation of SUs are performed simultaneously during the first transmission phase. The main objective is to improve the weighted sum-rate of the CRN through a joint optimization of the NOMA power coefficients and IRS phase adjustments during the second transmission phase. We propose an effective algorithm that breaks down the primary sum-rate maximization problem into two sub-problems where IRS phase shifts are computed once at the beginning of the algorithm. Through simulations, we demonstrate that the proposed algorithm yields substantial gains in the sum-rate performance compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: UAV-Assisted IoT Data Collection Scheme for IRS-Enabled Backscatter Communication Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Data collection schemes assisted by unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) play a key role in Internet-of-Things (IoT) networks. Nonetheless, the massive IoT devices bring new challenges, especially the high energy consumption. The backscatter communication (BackCom) technique can utilize ambient signals for passive transmission, thus being applicable to IoT systems. Due to its numerous reflecting elements, Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) can accomplish backscatter with high beamforming gain. Thus, IRS is suitable to alleviate the double-fading effect, which significantly restrains the development of BackCom networks. This paper utilizes the IRS-based BackCom technique to achieve efficient IoT data collection with the help of a UAV. The UAV provides carriers for multiple IRSs, which can emit data through backscatter. Then, the UAV collects the backward data dynamically. To maximize the collected data, the UAV’s transmit power, trajectory, and the IRS’s beamformers are jointly optimized. The optimization is realized through an alternative algorithm based on block coordinate descent (BCD) and reinforcement learning (RL). The Lagrangian dual transformation and semi-definite relaxation (SDR) approaches are employed to address the non-convexity of the problem effectively. Finally, simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed optimization scheme in the introduced system model.

articleTitle: Integrated Relay Selection and Power Allocation for Full-Duplex Relay Networks via Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Full-duplex (FD) systems enable users to simultaneously transmit and receive information on the same frequency, theoretically enhancing spectrum efficiency. However, the inherent openness and broadcasting nature of wireless communication pose significant security risks, especially in the presence of eavesdroppers. To enhance the reliability of FD relay systems, we derive the secrecy capacity of the systems and propose a novel approach that integrates relay selection and power allocation utilizing deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Specifically, our method employs deep Q network (DQN) and proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithms to jointly explore the optimal relay selection and power allocation strategies. Simulation results indicate that the developed approach enhances the average secrecy capacity by at least 30% compared to benchmark methods. Additionally, we assessed the performance of various methods under diverse conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness and adaptability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Accelerating Federated Learning With Model Segmentation for Edge Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of distributed learning strategies, Federated Learning (FL) stands out for its features such as model training on resource-constrained edge devices and high data security. However, the growing complexity of neural network models produces two challenges such as communication bottleneck and resource under-utilization, especially in edge networks. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces a novel framework by realizing the Parallel Communication-Computation Federated Learning Mode (P2CFed). Specifically, we design an adaptive layer-wise model segmentation strategy according to the wireless environments and computing capability of edge devices, which enables parallel training and transmission within different sub-models. In this way, parameter delivery takes place throughout the training process, thus considerably alleviating the communication overhead. Meanwhile, we also propose a joint optimization scheme with regard to the subchannel allocation, power control, and segmentation layer selection, which is then transformed into an iteration search process for obtaining optimal results. We have conducted extensive simulations to validate the effectiveness of P2CFed when compared with state-of-the-art benchmarks in terms of communication overhead and resource utilization. It also unveils that P2CFed brings a faster convergence rate and smaller training delay compared to traditional FL approaches.

articleTitle: Throughput Maximization Design for RIS-Assisted mmWave WPCN-NOMA Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: This paper considers an reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted millimeter-wave (mmWave) wireless-powered communication network (WPCN). In the network, multiple energy-constrained devices harvest radio frequency (RF) energy signals transmitted by the power station (PS) with the assistance of the RIS in the downlink (DL), and then transmit the signals to the data sink (DS) in the uplink (UL) employing non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) strategy. Under the considered framework, we aim to maximize the sum achievable throughput of all devices by jointly optimizing the device grouping, transmit power allocation of PS, energy beamforming vectors, and phase shift matrix of RIS in the DL transmission, as well as the phase shift matrix of RIS and transmission timeslot allocation for the UL transmission. To solve this non-convex problem with multiple high coupling parameters, the optimization problem is divided into three sub-problems. In the first sub-problem, an algorithm combining K-means++ clustering algorithm and exclusion theory is proposed to obtain optimal device grouping. For the second sub-problem, the transmit power allocation of PS, energy beamforming vectors, and phase shift matrix of RIS in the DL are obtained by alternating optimization (AO) algorithm. Then, we optimize the transmission timeslot allocation and phase shift matrix of RIS in the UL according to a successive convex approximation (SCA)-based 1-D search method in the third sub-problem. Numerical simulations verify the superiority of the proposed optimization scheme in improving the achievable throughput compared to other comparison schemes.

articleTitle: Joint Sleep Control and Energy Sharing Strategy With Deep Reinforcement Learning in Green Ultra-Dense Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: Ultra-dense network (UDN) is considered a viable solution to meet the growing demand for mobile data traffic. However, the massive deployment of small base stations (SBSs) dramatically increases the energy consumption and carbon footprint of the network, posing significant environmental challenges. In this paper, we design a green UDN system driven by renewable energy sources (RES) that utilizes sleep control and energy sharing methods to reduce grid energy consumption and enhance the utilization of RES. To address the dynamic variations in harvested RES and traffic load arrivals, we propose a joint sleep control and energy sharing strategy based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Specifically, we formulate the sleep control and energy sharing problem as a markov decision process (MDP), which can be solved using DRL. To tackle the exponentially growing action space associated with the number of SBSs, we develop an SBS energy management algorithm based on multi-discrete proximal policy optimization (PPO) with a multi-dimensional action space output. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our proposed scheme significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of energy efficiency in green UDNs.

articleTitle: Mobility-Aware User Association and Computation Offloading in Ultra-Dense Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking
abstract: The integration of mobile edge computing (MEC) into ultra-dense network (UDN) has emerged as a promising solution for providing uninterrupted task offloading services to computation-demanding mobile devices (MDs), leveraging densely deployed MEC servers. However, the mobility of MDs can significantly affect the computation offloading decision and system performance in UDN-MEC. To address this issue, we develop a joint optimization algorithm for mobility-aware user association and computation offloading to minimizize the total system cost, including delay and energy consumption in UDN-MEC. Specifically, a polynomial fitting algorithm based on an extended Kalman filter (PFA-EKF) is designed to predict the nonlinear moving trajectories of the MDs. Furthermore, we present a mobility-aware user-association rule based on a breadth-first search (UAR-BFS) that can realize balanced matching offloading in the overlapping coverage area of densely deployed small base stations. Accordingly, we propose an improved deep deterministic policy gradient-based greedy algorithm (IDDPG-GA) to address the joint optimization problem of multiuser dynamic offloading and resource allocation, in which an intelligently adjusted bias factor is proposed to enhance collaborative behavior among MDs. Extensive numerical results and comparisons demonstrate the promising performance improvements of the proposed scheme compared with existing benchmark schemes in various scenarios.
